review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read CoverAssembly.lean (exists_section_of_cover_and_coprime and hopfMultiplier_quotient), SL2CentrallyClosed.lean (hopfMultiplierToKer_bijective), and POmegaPlusMultiplier.lean and POmegaMinusMultiplier.lean. Those two files repeat the same tail, which shows the pattern is wider than this file. The only duplication I found in this file is the tail shared by the two big theorems. The earlier setup lines (CharP, perfectness and finiteness of the spin group) are similar but depend on different quadratic-form API, so I left them out. I did not check that the proposed lemma compiles. Its hypotheses are chosen to match the instances the two proofs already use: Finite H, Group.IsPerfect H, and Finite X obtained from the surjection. The remaining uncertainty is where the lemma should live and whether Finite X should be a hypothesis or derived inside.

findings.problem: Both theorems repeat the same non-trivial argument and differ only in the group and in the final identification of q.ker. The shared steps are: (1) the quotient is perfect via Group.IsPerfect.ofSurjective hq, and commutator = ⊤ follows; (2) the quotient is finite via Finite.of_surjective; (3) HopfCover is finite via finite_hopfCover; (4) the Hopf multiplier is isomorphic to q.ker via MulEquiv.ofBijective applied to hopfMultiplierToKer_bijective; (5) the result is composed with hopfMultiplierEquivGriess. Lines 48-51 and 61-67 in the plus case match lines 95-98 and 112-118 in the minus case, with the types renamed. The same block also appears in POmegaPlusMultiplier.lean (pomegaPlus_hopfMultiplier), POmegaMinusMultiplier.lean (pomegaMinus_hopfMultiplier), and other multiplier files. The file's own CoverAssembly.hopfMultiplier_quotient is the special case q = mk', but there is no general version for an arbitrary central-kernel surjection.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in CoverAssembly, next to hopfMultiplier_quotient, which that lemma could then follow from. Statement: for H X : Type with [Group H] [Finite H] [Group.IsPerfect H] [Group X] and q : H →* X, hq : Function.Surjective q, hker : q.ker ≤ Subgroup.center H, and hsplit : ∀ (E : Type) [Group E] [Finite E] (π : E →* H), Function.Surjective π → π.ker ≤ Subgroup.center E → ∃ σ : H →* E, ∀ g, π (σ g) = g, the conclusion is commutator X = ⊤ ∧ Nonempty (CFSG.Open.griessHopfMultiplier X ≃* q.ker). Proof sketch: set hperf := Group.IsPerfect.ofSurjective hq and get Finite X from Finite.of_surjective q hq. Obtain Finite (HopfCover X) from finite_hopfCover hperf. Then take e1 := MulEquiv.ofBijective _ (SL2Closed.hopfMultiplierToKer_bijective q hq hker fun π hπ hcen => hsplit _ π hπ hcen), and return ⟨Group.IsPerfect.commutator_eq_top, ⟨(hopfMultiplierEquivGriess _).trans e1⟩⟩. In this file, after hsplit is built, the plus theorem becomes: obtain ⟨hc, ⟨e⟩⟩ := CoverAssembly.hopfMultiplier_equiv_ker q hq hker.le hsplit, then exact ⟨hc, ⟨e.trans ((MulEquiv.subgroupCongr hkerZ).trans e3)⟩⟩. The minus theorem does the same with (zmodCyclicMulEquiv hcyc).symm in place of e3, keeping its existing rw [← hcard]. Under their actual hypotheses: hsplit is already available in both theorems (from exists_section_of_cover_and_coprime), Finite H comes from the existing finite_spinGroup_of_ker instance, and Group.IsPerfect H comes from the existing isPerfect_spinGroup_* instance. Both hypotheses are already in scope at the point of use. This also removes the local hperf, Finite X, Finite HopfCover and e1 declarations from both proofs.
findings.benefit: Each theorem would keep only its group-specific content: the section-existence cases and the identification of the kernel. The generic Hopf-cover bookkeeping would be proved once, so a future change (for example to hopfMultiplierToKer_bijective) would be made once, not in every multiplier file that repeats this tail. It also reduces the risk that the plus and minus variants drift apart.
